svg.text: Глава 4 · Стандартизация и классификация сетей
Олифер, 7-е изд. · RAG p0108:c01–p0130:c01 · PDF 108–130 · printed 107–129
1 · Decomposition and protocol stack
Complex interaction → modules → hierarchical layers
Service interface: adjacent layers inside one node
Protocol: same-level peer entities on different nodes
Stack: enough hierarchically organized protocols for interaction
Model says what · protocol says how · implementation realizes it
2 · OSI seven-layer reference model
7 Application · user-facing network services
6 Presentation · data representation / syntax / encryption
5 Session · dialogue / synchronization checkpoints
4 Transport · required transport-service quality
3 Network · end-to-end nodes / forwarding / route
2 Data Link · adjacent nodes / frames · 1 Physical · signals/bits
3 · Encapsulation and node roles
Sender: message moves down, each layer adds service information
Receiver: each layer processes/removes its header, passes data upward
End host → full stack
Repeater → physical · LAN switch → physical+link
Router → physical+link+network · additional service protocols may exist
4 · Vertical layers + horizontal planes
User plane → user traffic
Control plane → routing / connection setup / naming information
Management plane → administration / monitoring information
Source example: RIP/OSPF show strict OSI layer mapping can be awkward
OSI works better as reference vocabulary than literal implementation template
5 · Standardization and openness
Open specification = published + public + agreed standard specification
Benefits: multi-vendor interoperability · component replacement · network coupling
Sources: vendor · committees/associations · national · international
Internet: RFC process · ISOC / IAB / IRTF / IETF in source description
TCP/IP: many upper/lower choices · IP as common narrow waist
Current-status claims remain source snapshots under RAG-only policy
6 · Classification: independent axes
Coverage → LAN / MAN / WAN
Medium → wired / wireless
Switching → packets / circuits · forwarding variant
Topology → full mesh / tree / star / ring / mixed
Users → carrier / corporate / personal
Role → access / aggregation / backbone · primary / overlay
Practical reading rule
Do not ask “what OSI layer is this?” before identifying the actual function, protocol and node role.
Do not classify a network by one label only: geographic scope, medium, switching, ownership and role are different axes.
No executable CLI is supplied by the chapter.
Chapter 5 starts at p0131:c01 · reading state unchanged · source extraction findings recorded separately.
